solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Crustacean in pub clean when cooked

indicators.note: cooking changes food into a new form, so the word before it gets rearranged

explanation.surface: A seafood dish at the local, served spotless once it has been cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a pub kitchen, which makes 'cooked' read as food prep rather than an instruction to rearrange CLEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnacles are small marine creatures that cling to rocks and hulls, belonging to the crustacean class like crabs.

clue.text: Robert has been ahead in Olympic event

blocks.note: Bob is the short form of Robert
to have been ahead is to have led

explanation.surface: An athlete called Robert has been leading in some Olympic contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has' becomes the contraction 's, so Robert has reads as BOB'S, a trick that recurs often in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing sleds down an icy track is a Winter Games sport, contested by teams of two or four riders.

clue.text: Cow perhaps having drink at home with insect

blocks.note: rum is a spirit, so a drink

explanation.surface: A cow sharing a drink at home with a bug for company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals that a cow is only one example of the answer, a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattle chew the cud, bringing food back up from a multi-chambered stomach, which is what classes animals like them.

clue.text: This won’t turn in the lock

definitions.text: This won’t turn in the lock

blocks.clueFragment: This won’t turn in the lock
blocks.note: surface reading: a key that jams and will not turn in a door lock

blocks.clueFragment: This won’t turn in the lock
blocks.note: setter's reading: a long narrow vessel sitting in a waterway lock chamber, with no room to turn around

explanation.walkthrough: A lock is also the gated chamber on a waterway, and a long narrowboat fits one so snugly that it could never turn round inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow vessels built for inland waterways pass through locks, chambers that raise or lower them between water levels.

clue.text: Grounded winger involved in three murders

indicators.note: something involved in a phrase is caught up inside its letters

blocks.note: thrEE MUrders, spanning the word break

explanation.surface: A disgraced footballer implicated in three killings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests a football player and 'grounded' a punishment, but here it is a bird with wings that cannot fly.
explanation.definitionFit: The large Australian bird has wings yet cannot fly, so it stays on the ground.

clue.text: Reasonable travel cost announced

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so we go by its sound

blocks.note: a fare is the price of a journey

explanation.surface: A statement that ticket prices are sensible.
explanation.walkthrough: The cost of a journey is a fare, which sounds exactly like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something just, even-handed and acceptable, so they are synonyms here.

clue.text: Force to slam explosively causing wreckage

indicators.note: an explosion blows things apart, so the letters beside it are scattered

blocks.note: F is the physics abbreviation for force

explanation.surface: A violent blow that leaves debris everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: F for force comes first, then the six letters of TO SLAM are rearranged after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Floating debris from a ship lost at sea is the classic sense, paired often with jetsam.

clue.text: Here in France, head shows hostile attitude

blocks.note: a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Inverness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: A French boss displaying an unfriendly manner.
explanation.walkthrough: A head, or headland, is a ness, a word found in British place names such as Dungeness on the Kent coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Coldness of manner, a frosty unwelcoming reception, describes someone being unfriendly towards another.

clue.text: British crowd returned device for detonation

indicators.note: returning means going back the way you came, so the letters of both words run backwards

explanation.surface: A British crowd came back with an explosive.
explanation.walkthrough: B and MOB are written together first, then the whole string runs backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An explosive weapon is built to be set off, which is what detonating means.

clue.text: Obsession, not initially serious, developed

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it
something developed has been worked into a new shape, so the word before it is reshaped

explanation.surface: A fixation that started out trivial and grew worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not initially' reads like a phrase meaning 'at first it wasn't', but it just asks for N.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsessive fixation is one kind of anxious mental disorder, the broad clinical label for such conditions.

clue.text: Arthurian knight taking his weapon back to lake

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the two words that follow run backwards together

blocks.note: a knight's weapon is a lance

explanation.surface: A knight of the Round Table returning a weapon to a lake, like Excalibur.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes Excalibur going back to the Lady of the Lake, but 'back' reverses the two words after it, not the weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Lancelot was the foremost knight of King Arthur's Round Table in the legends.

clue.text: Will roused mates in canvas shelter

indicators.note: roused people are stirred up, so the word after it is stirred into a new order
one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: a tent is a shelter made of canvas

explanation.surface: Someone named Will wakes up friends who are camping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' at the start looks like a man's name, but it is the legal document.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's last written wishes about their property is formally called their last will and testament.

clue.text: Hoofed mammal in Kansas occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of kAnSaS

explanation.surface: A hoofed animal seen now and then in the American state of Kansas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occasionally' reads as how often the animal is seen, but it picks the even letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey is an animal with hooves, and the older word for a donkey is this.

clue.text: Fish holding short stick in biannual event

indicators.note: something short is missing a bit at the end, so the word after it loses its last letter
to hold something is to have it inside you

explanation.surface: A fish clutching a stick at some twice-yearly occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: Biannual means twice a year, and the sun reaches its highest and lowest points once each in June and December.
explanation.definitionFit: The longest and shortest days fall in June and December, so this astronomical moment happens twice every year.

clue.text: Manic Monday for energetic person

indicators.note: manic suggests wild frenzied behaviour, so the next word is thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A hectic start to the week suits a go-getter, echoing the song title 'Manic Monday'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manic Monday' is a familiar song title, so it reads as one phrase rather than instruction plus fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A generator produces power, and figuratively a lively, forceful go-getter is called by the same name.

clue.text: Get any in arrangement with Zulu banker?

indicators.note: an arrangement sets things out in a chosen order, so the letters are re-ordered

blocks.note: Zulu is Z in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Trying to strike a deal with a South African financier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' is a crossword favourite for a river, the thing that has banks; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: China's longest waterway flows between banks, making it jokingly something that has banks.

clue.text: Mister Solo shot after a little hesitation?

indicators.note: something shot is ruined or wrecked, so the word before it is broken up
after tells us the rearranged word follows the other pieces

blocks.note: er is a small pause in speech

explanation.surface: Han Solo fires his blaster after a moment's pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mister Solo' reads as Han Solo, but 'Mister' stands alone as the definition: something that produces a mist.
explanation.definitionFit: A spray can releases a fine mist, so it is jokingly a thing that mists.

clue.text: Prophet in South Africa fried pastry

indicators.note: a person in a country is inside it

blocks.note: Amos is an Old Testament prophet

explanation.surface: A holy man in South Africa eating a fried snack.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bible's minor prophets, such as Amos, Hosea and Micah, are common crossword supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: The triangular Indian snack is a spiced filling wrapped in dough and deep-fried.

clue.text: Entertainer is treat when sozzled

indicators.note: sozzled means drunk, and a drunk's words come out jumbled

explanation.surface: A performer who is great fun after a few drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Sozzled is British slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional performer such as a singer or dancer on stage is often given this slightly grand name.

clue.text: Mischievous goddess had some food

blocks.note: the Greek goddess of mischief, folly and ruin
past tense of the verb for having a meal

explanation.surface: A naughty goddess snacking.
explanation.walkthrough: Ate is a minor figure of Greek myth who led gods and mortals into folly; the everyday verb is the easier half.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek deity of folly and ruin bears this name, and it is also the past tense of eating.

clue.text: Instruct class producing toy

blocks.note: to train someone is to instruct them
a set is a class or group, as in school sets

explanation.surface: A teacher's lesson that ends up making a plaything.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools pupils are grouped by ability into sets, so class and set match.
explanation.definitionFit: Model railway track with engines and carriages is a children's plaything and hobbyists' collectible.

clue.text: Lug instrument and books round room

blocks.note: OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books

explanation.surface: Hauling a musical instrument and a pile of books around a room.
explanation.walkthrough: Lug is British slang for an ear, not the verb to carry; the instrument is medical, not musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors use this lighted device to look inside the ear canal and at the eardrum.

clue.text: Blade beheaded wild pig

indicators.note: losing a head means losing the top, so the opening letter of the animal goes

blocks.note: a boar is a wild pig

explanation.surface: A sword cutting the head off a wild pig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blade' suggests a weapon, but rowers also call their oars blades.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat end of a rowing pole is its blade, and rowers use that word for the whole thing.

clue.text: Cash card number son secures

blocks.note: a personal identification number for a bank card

explanation.surface: A son guards the code for a bank card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Secures' sits at the end as a verb, the definition, not an action the son performs.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten something in place with a pin is to fix it firmly, a verb meaning fasten.

clue.text: Man will encounter wicked souls here

explanation.surface: A warning about where a man will meet evildoers.
explanation.walkthrough: HE plus the contraction 'LL gives HE'LL; the definition is the place where the wicked end up.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinners' souls are said to be damned to this underworld of punishment in Christian belief.

clue.text: Rescue dog losing tail

indicators.note: a tail is the end of something, so the breed name drops its last letter

blocks.note: a gundog breed, such as the Labrador or golden, that fetches shot game

explanation.surface: A rescue dog that has lost its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rescue dog' reads as one phrase, but 'Rescue' is the definition and the dog is a gundog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: To get something back from where it was lost is to save it, so the verbs are synonyms.
